main_text.l: EXERC. XXXII.
VTRVM EPILEPSIA SIT
VENTRICVLORVM cerebri obstructio?
AN uero morbus comitialis & fonticus sit uentriculorum cerebri obstructio, nonnulli non abs re dubitant.
Si (inquiunt) obstruerentur cerebri finus,
sensu & motu plane priuaret animal: quan-
doquidem sentiendi facultas, ac mouendi,
seu spiritus animalis in singula membra
haudquaquam diffunderetur, sed intus prę-
cluderetur. At uero singulis epilepsiæ pa-
roxysmis epilepticorum membra uehemen-
tiori motu, quàm antea concitantur. Quod
autem deprauatę moueantur, nō penuria,
facultatis animalis, sed cerebri læsio in cau-
sa est. Etenim ipsum læsum omnibus mem-
bris confusę, deprauateq; imperat, necfin-
gulis musculis quantum extendi, laxariq;
debeat, præfinit. Idem sane ipsi adest, quòd
& facuo, aut insano regi, qui suos subditos
deprauatę regit, ac miserrimè concutit. Ita-
que his omnibus rite perpensis, nullam fie-
ri finuū cerebri obstructionem in comitia-
li morbo, concludere
rectè possumus. Ad-
hæc in forti apoplexia, & etiam in debili
omnes

page.notes: Transcription is from a faint, slightly blurred scan. The text was read with care but several words are uncertain and should be checked against the original. Note that the printed text reads "facuo" and "fingulis" and other forms as set; these are copied as the printer seems to have set them, with no emendation. The phrase "Quod" after "Quoniam" and "uentriculorum" are read as printed. The line "omnes" at the foot is a catchword-like word at the right margin and is kept in the text as the last printed word. A few words at line ends, such as "fonti-cus", "comitia-li", "deprauatę", are set with printed hyphens or broken across lines and may need confirmation of exact hyphenation. The transcription has not been checked letter by letter against a higher-resolution scan.
